difficulty_model.name: Minetti et al. 2002 energy cost of running
difficulty_model.description: Energy cost of running at this grade divided by the cost on flat ground (1.0 = flat; 1.5 = 50% more energy per meter). Valid for grades from -45% to +45%.

sources.licence: Which streets the course uses: facts from the organizer. Street geometry: OpenStreetMap (ODbL)

sources.title: 2017 NYC 1-foot bare-earth DEM (City of New York topobathymetric LiDAR), via NOAA Digital Coast
sources.licence: NYC Open Data: no restrictions on use (NYC Admin. Code § 23-504); NOAA redistribution, no access constraints
sources.note: Bare earth: buildings, trees and bridge decks removed. NAVD88 heights, converted from US survey feet to meters.

sources.title: 2017 NYC Topobathymetric LiDAR (City of New York), via NOAA Digital Coast
sources.licence: NYC Open Data: no restrictions on use (NYC Admin. Code § 23-504); NOAA redistribution, no access constraints
sources.note: Collected May 2017, ~50% leaf-off. Class 17 (bridge deck) returns give deck heights; NAVD88 (GEOID18) meters.

sources.title: Earth Gravitational Model 2008 (EGM2008), 2.5-minute worldwide geoid height grid (U.S. National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency)
sources.licence: Public domain: a work of a U.S. federal agency, labelled so in the file and by the PROJ project that redistributes it (NGA's own page states no terms)
sources.note: How far sea level is above the WGS84 ellipsoid. Added to each height above sea level to get the height the 3D scene needs. Read from https://cdn.proj.org/us_nga_egm08_25.tif (a GeoTIFF the PROJ project made from the model), between the four grid points around each place. Against the cities' official models it is 0.21 m high in Berlin (GCG2016) and about 0.37 m high in New York (GEOID18 and the step from NAD83 to WGS84).

sources.title: OpenStreetMap (course streets and bridge locations along the course)
Building Footprints (BUILDING) — City of New York, Office of Technology and Innovation
sources.licence: NYC Open Data: no restrictions on use (NYC Admin. Code § 23-504)
sources.note: Outline, the ground at the building's foot (GROUND_ELEVATION, NAVD88) and the roof's height above that ground (HEIGHT_ROOF), both in US survey feet; field definitions at https://github.com/CityOfNewYork/nyc-geo-metadata/blob/master/Metadata/Metadata_BuildingFootprints.md. Read only along the course corridor. The city captures buildings over 400 sq ft and 12 ft tall; a record whose roof height is zero or missing is one the city never worked out, and is not drawn, as are the placeholder triangles it uses for a building it has no picture of yet.

sources.title: NOAA Solar Calculator (US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration): the equations for the sun's position
sources.licence: Work of the US government: public domain
sources.note: Geometric position, without the bending of light near the horizon: what casts a shadow.
